methods.name: 5W2H
methods.purpose: Clarify an insufficiently defined problem.
methods.when: Clarify an insufficiently defined problem.
methods.pitfall: An answer is not a verified cause.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Clarify where picking errors occur.

methods.name: Is / Is Not
methods.purpose: Compare affected and unaffected situations.
methods.when: Compare affected and unaffected situations.
methods.pitfall: Differences suggest tests, not causality.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Compare errors on two pick lanes.

methods.name: Gemba observation
methods.purpose: Understand work at the place it happens.
methods.when: Understand work at the place it happens.
methods.pitfall: Do not turn observation into blame.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Observe a pallet handoff.

methods.name: Voice of Customer / CTQ
methods.purpose: Translate customer needs into checkable conditions.
methods.when: Translate customer needs into checkable conditions.
methods.pitfall: Confirm the translation with the customer.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Translate on-time delivery into a defined cut-off measure.

methods.name: SIPOC
methods.purpose: Set high-level process boundaries and handoffs.
methods.when: Set high-level process boundaries and handoffs.
methods.pitfall: A high-level map omits operational detail.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Map receipt-to-putaway.

methods.name: Ishikawa / fishbone
methods.purpose: Organize possible causes of a defined effect.
methods.when: Organize possible causes of a defined effect.
methods.pitfall: The diagram does not prove root causes.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Explore damage during outbound handling.

methods.name: 5 Whys
methods.purpose: Trace a gap beyond its immediate symptom.
methods.when: Trace a gap beyond its immediate symptom.
methods.pitfall: Five is a starting aid, not a required endpoint.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Trace recurring label reprints.

methods.name: Brainstorming
methods.purpose: Generate options before selecting a solution.
methods.when: Generate options before selecting a solution.
methods.pitfall: Popularity is not evidence.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Collect ideas to reduce scanner searching.

methods.name: Affinity diagram
methods.purpose: Group many observations by related themes.
methods.when: Group many observations by related themes.
methods.pitfall: Grouping demonstrates similarity, not causality.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Group picking feedback by theme.

methods.name: Relations diagram
methods.purpose: Explore dependencies between interacting factors.
methods.when: Explore dependencies between interacting factors.
methods.pitfall: An arrow alone does not establish cause.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Explore workload and rework dependencies.

methods.name: Tree diagram
methods.purpose: Break a broad objective into workable parts.
methods.when: Break a broad objective into workable parts.
methods.pitfall: Hierarchy is a planning structure.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Break damage reduction into tests.

methods.name: Flowchart / swimlane
methods.purpose: Understand sequence, decisions and responsibility.
methods.when: Understand sequence, decisions and responsibility.
methods.pitfall: Measure times; a map is not a simulation.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Map goods receipt across roles.

methods.name: Current / future value-stream map
methods.purpose: See material and information flow across a stream.
methods.when: See material and information flow across a stream.
methods.pitfall: Same-unit sums are descriptive; do not imply a validated future state.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Map inbound pallets to available stock.

methods.name: Spaghetti diagram
methods.purpose: Expose walking or movement paths.
methods.when: Expose walking or movement paths.
methods.pitfall: Straight segments approximate distance; obstacles and routes need observation.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Trace a picker collecting packaging.

methods.name: Waste analysis
methods.purpose: Identify activities consuming resources without customer value.
methods.when: Identify activities consuming resources without customer value.
methods.pitfall: Required safety or compliance work cannot be removed by labeling it waste.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Record waiting at a loading dock.

methods.name: Check sheet / tally
methods.purpose: Collect repeatable event counts.
methods.when: Collect repeatable event counts.
methods.pitfall: Changing definitions invalidates comparisons.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Count damaged cartons by shift.

methods.name: Pareto
methods.purpose: Prioritize measured categories by contribution.
methods.when: Prioritize measured categories by contribution.
methods.pitfall: The 80% line is a reference, not a guaranteed 80/20 law.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Compare picking error counts by type.

methods.name: Stratification
methods.purpose: Compare data from distinct operational groups.
methods.when: Compare data from distinct operational groups.
methods.pitfall: Group differences do not explain their cause.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Compare pick duration by zone.

methods.name: Histogram
methods.purpose: Inspect the distribution of numeric data.
methods.when: Inspect the distribution of numeric data.
methods.pitfall: Small samples and chosen bins can mislead; no normality claim.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Inspect loading duration.

methods.name: Scatterplot
methods.purpose: Explore association between paired numeric measures.
methods.when: Explore association between paired numeric measures.
methods.pitfall: Correlation does not establish causality.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Compare queue length and waiting time.

methods.name: Run chart
methods.purpose: See how a measure changes over time.
methods.when: See how a measure changes over time.
methods.pitfall: This plot makes no automatic special-cause significance claim.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Track daily dispatch delays.

methods.name: Control chart (I–MR)
methods.purpose: Explore continuous individual observations using I–MR limits.
methods.when: Explore continuous individual observations using I–MR limits.
methods.pitfall: Limits are estimated process variation, not targets/specifications. Only I–MR is implemented; no attribute/subgroup charts.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Inspect consecutive carton-weight observations.

methods.name: Boxplot
methods.purpose: Compare median, quartiles and spread across groups.
methods.when: Compare median, quartiles and spread across groups.
methods.pitfall: Tukey whiskers and linear-interpolation quartiles are descriptive.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Compare unloading duration across shifts.

methods.name: Impact / effort matrix
methods.purpose: Discuss practical options against impact and effort.
methods.when: Discuss practical options against impact and effort.
methods.pitfall: Local scores are subjective and not CEVA policy.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Compare scanner placement options.

methods.name: Weighted decision matrix
methods.purpose: Compare options using explicit weighted criteria.
methods.when: Compare options using explicit weighted criteria.
methods.pitfall: Weights and scores require judgment; missing criteria block ranking.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Compare two packaging systems.

methods.name: FMEA
methods.purpose: Examine failure modes and planned controls.
methods.when: Examine failure modes and planned controls.
methods.pitfall: RPN is only a local screening aid; high severity needs attention regardless of RPN.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Review wrong-item shipment failure modes.

methods.name: Poka-Yoke
methods.purpose: Prevent errors or make them immediately detectable.
methods.when: Prevent errors or make them immediately detectable.
steps: Design a prevention or detection test
methods.pitfall: A reminder alone is not proven error prevention.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Test a barcode mismatch interlock.

methods.name: 5S
methods.purpose: Build a workplace standard that makes problems visible.
methods.when: Build a workplace standard that makes problems visible.
steps: Observe each of the five components
methods.pitfall: Local 0 = absent, 1 = partly demonstrated, 2 = demonstrated; not a TCA classification.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Organize the packing station and check sustain.

methods.name: Red-tag register
methods.purpose: Track decisions on unnecessary workplace items.
methods.when: Track decisions on unnecessary workplace items.
methods.pitfall: Do not dispose of safety/compliance assets without authority.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Review unused packaging fixtures.

methods.name: Visual-management standard
methods.purpose: Make normal and abnormal conditions actionable.
methods.when: Make normal and abnormal conditions actionable.
methods.pitfall: A board without a response routine does not improve performance.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Show the dock queue and escalation owner.

methods.name: Kanban / pull / WIP
methods.purpose: Control work release through explicit downstream demand.
methods.when: Control work release through explicit downstream demand.
steps: Set and test local WIP limits
methods.pitfall: A board alone does not create pull; limits are local experiments.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Test replenishment signals for cartons.

methods.name: Takt / cycle-time analysis
methods.purpose: Compare actual cycle times with customer demand pace.
methods.when: Compare actual cycle times with customer demand pace.
steps: Define net available time and demand for the same period
methods.pitfall: Demand must be positive; all times must share the selected unit.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Compare packing cycles with shift demand.

methods.name: Yamazumi / work balancing
methods.purpose: Balance work elements relative to takt.
methods.when: Balance work elements relative to takt.
methods.pitfall: Summed elements assume sequential work; overlap requires separate analysis.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Balance tasks across two pack stations.

methods.name: SMED
methods.purpose: Reduce changeover by separating internal and external work.
methods.when: Reduce changeover by separating internal and external work.
methods.pitfall: A proposed duration is not a realized saving.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Move label preparation outside a line stop.

methods.name: Heijunka worksheet
methods.purpose: Plan a leveled mix and volume over time.
methods.when: Plan a leveled mix and volume over time.
methods.pitfall: A level plan needs stable capability and cannot erase demand variability.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Plan a repeatable outbound service mix.

methods.name: Standard work
methods.purpose: Describe the best current agreed work sequence.
methods.when: Describe the best current agreed work sequence.
methods.pitfall: A document alone does not demonstrate adoption.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Agree a repeatable label-check sequence.

methods.name: TWI job instruction
methods.purpose: Teach a job consistently and safely.
methods.when: Teach a job consistently and safely.
steps: Demonstrate and practice steps with key points and reasons
Follow up until competence is shown
methods.pitfall: Attendance alone is not competence.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Teach pallet wrapping at point of use.

methods.name: Control / sustain plan
methods.purpose: Keep a proven change effective over time.
methods.when: Keep a proven change effective over time.
methods.pitfall: This is an operational plan, not a statistical control-limit calculation.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Check barcode scan adherence.

methods.name: Leader standard work
methods.purpose: Support improvement through a repeatable leadership routine.
methods.when: Support improvement through a repeatable leadership routine.
methods.pitfall: Checking a box does not establish capability.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Review the daily dock handoff.

methods.name: Kamishibai checks
methods.purpose: Rotate visible checks of agreed work standards.
methods.when: Rotate visible checks of agreed work standards.
methods.pitfall: A green card needs an actual observation.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Check a sample of dispatch handoffs.

methods.name: Toyota Kata experiment
methods.purpose: Learn toward a target condition through small experiments.
methods.when: Learn toward a target condition through small experiments.
steps: Compare outcome and decide the next step
methods.pitfall: Do not rewrite a prediction after seeing the result.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Test a different pick-route sequence.

methods.name: TPM / OEE
methods.purpose: Separate availability, performance and quality losses.
methods.when: Separate availability, performance and quality losses.
steps: Define scheduled time and ideal cycle
Use loss evidence to plan TPM work
methods.pitfall: Use the same time unit; invalid speed/output relationships are flagged, not capped.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Measure conveyor availability and defects.

methods.name: DMAIC guidance
methods.purpose: Guide a data-based improvement within this PDCA event.
methods.when: Guide a data-based improvement within this PDCA event.
steps: Map phases to existing event data
Check the evidence at each decision
methods.pitfall: Guidance references the same event; it does not certify Six Sigma completion.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Guide a recurring dispatch-delay investigation.

methods.name: 8D guidance
methods.purpose: Guide containment and corrective action in the existing event.
methods.when: Guide containment and corrective action in the existing event.
methods.pitfall: Containment and permanent correction differ; no duplicate event dossier.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Guide an incorrect-shipment corrective action.

methods.name: DOE experiment planning
methods.purpose: Plan controlled trials of factors and interactions.
methods.when: Plan controlled trials of factors and interactions.
methods.pitfall: Planning only: no automatic significance, causal or optimum conclusion.
methods.example: Fictional logistics example: Plan safe packaging trials with two controlled factors.
